Although the initial application felt wonderful on my arm, where I test products, the smell was intolerable for me, and I had to wipe it off. title: Disappointed - went back to my T800
text:
I bought a T800 quite a few years ago when I found the Austrian-made unit on sale at the local Target store. It lasted very well, and I was somewhat disappointed when the battery eventually would no longer accept a charge, though it continued to work while plugged in.
After carefully looking into alternatives, I went with a T970 from Amazon.com, hoping for the same quality. Major letdown! This Chinese-made unit just is not up to the same standard as my T800. The charger is a seperate seperate and bulky transformer, instead of the simple cord of the T800. The T970 is larger, more awkward to hold and to use, and more fragile in every possible way. The vacuum, which was one of the initial attractions, works, but only marginally well, and the unit is unstable when laid down on a solid surface. If the mile-long charging cord is attached, expect to have to prop the unit against a wall to prevent it rolling over.
I spent $6.00 on a top-quality replacement cell for my T800 (shipping was $4.00, for a 700mA Sanyo AA), and after careful disassembly and reassembly, successfully replaced the ailing cell without breaking anything. Unbelievably, The T800 now outlasts the T970 two-fold.
I wish I'd stuck it out with the T800 in the first place.
.
Updated June 29, 2009.
After about two years of irregular use and the resulting regular complete self-discharges, the T970 stopped functioning even while plugged in, unless first given time to recharge. Initial time to start working after plugging in has increased to the point where it no longer works even being plugged in for 24 hours.

title: Authentic mink is never cruelty free
text: I'm sorry that this isn't review, but I think other animal lovers need to know: "cruelty free mink" is a lie. Farmers have been caught lying about "getting the hairs by gently brushing the minks". They don't want to pay to house and feed minks that they can only get less than a handful of hairs from each day. It is cheaper and faster to kill the animal and harvest the fur from the pelt. title: NOT a nail buffer - this is a file - worth maybe $8 so way over-priced
text: A nail buffer requires a very, very, very fine grit so it will polish and shine the nail. This supposed buffer is medium grit, which means it is good for filing nail edges and maybe ok for removing ridges from the nail surface if you use very light pressure, but it will not polish the nail top surface - i.e. despite the name, this is a file.  When used on the nail top surface, it mostly produces scratches. Even if the grit on this file was fine enough, it is too wide to properly polish the small curved surface of a nail (I am not talking thickness/height here, I mean width).  Plus decorative top is just glued on.  I have tried so many glass nail buffers that I have lost count - all were too wide and too coarse to actually buff the nail except one - the one that actually had a fine enough grit was so wide that it could only polish my nails in spots.  I would love a long-lasting glass nail buffer, but at this point my conclusion is that glass is not suitable for buffing because it is too rigid and all supposed glass buffers available are very badly designed.  I give up.  I guess I will continue with disposable 4-sided soft block buffers - at least those work properly.  Gave the file to my niece as she loves the appearance of it and it is good for filing (properly etched, medium grit), just way over-priced at $13 and NOT as described.

text:
So I’ve been following manscaped for a couple of years and have always been interested in their products, both on design, their specifications, and their advertising.

I was honestly pretty dissatisfied by both the Lawnmower and their nose tool. I’ll give my personal non biased pros and cons on the Lawnmower because that’s where I would like to discuss my experience.

Lawnmower Pros: the battery life is amazing, I haven’t charged mine in a month and it still has battery life. Also the led light is very bright and convenient. The design is very modern and sleek, easy to hold use, and it extremely quiet.

Cons: the blade is not as skin proof as advertised, and when wet the bottom guide tugs making
It not very maneuverable. Secondly I whole heartedly belive I was mislead by the amount leftover from using it. It leaves behind at least a 1/16th amount of hair that you would have to go over again with a razor due to the blade not being able to get close enough. Why advertise a product knowing it can’t shave baby smooth like advertised?

Overall, for the price it’s definitely a great buy, the pros do outweigh the cons to some extent. But In the end a razor is much more effective and less of a chance for nipping yourself. Until they come out with a stubble remover, I don’t think this would be a product you’d want if you prefer smooth and no stubble.

title: Went for the full experience - went home disappointed
text:
I ordered the full line of the OZ Naturals products, I have normal to oily combination skin and here are the results after 30 days:

** Vitamin C Serum - No difference. It was so thin and runny, I'm not sure it did anything for my skin. Will be throwing this away as it's past the 30 day return policy.

** Facial Mask - This was supposed to be hydrating, but I found that it dried my face out terribly. I couldn't keep it on for the minimum time suggested because my face started to hurt from the drying feeling. Will be throwing this away as it's past the 30 day return policy.

** Scrub For Your Face - This was OK, but a little drying. I expected that since it's a scrub. Will keep this product and use every once and awhile.

** Facial Cleanser (orange bottle) - OMG this was SO drying! Yes, it does make the face smooth, but when you combine this with the toner and the moisturizer, it looked like I was in the sun all day because my face was bright red. Will be throwing this away as it's past the 30 day return policy.

** Facial Toner - The bottle says to use this after the shower to "lock in moisture". I didn't feel like my skin was any more moisturized. In fact, it didn't feel like anything. If I used this alone or with a "non-OZ" moisturizer, I was OK. If combined with 2 other products, it was like the trinity of hell for my face. Will be throwing this away as it's past the 30 day return policy.

** Facial Moisturizer (blue one with sea kelp) - Yea...went on smooth, but then my face felt "stiff" after it absorbed the moisturizer. After the sunburn experience, I tried again with just the face wash/moisturizer combo and I needed an additional moisturizer, so my face didn't feel like it was going to "crack". Will be throwing this away as it's past the 30 day return policy.

Combining the face wash, toner, and moisturizer -
This got me twice - once I thought maybe I did something wrong and it took after sun aloe to make my face stop burning. The 2nd time I cursed my stupidity at trying again and will not use that combination (or the products because they will be going in the trash) again. I tried several different combinations of these products and was always met with 1 of 2 results - the fiery depths of hell on my face or feeling like my face was so dry I was standing in full sun in the desert. Neither was a pleasant experience for me.

I know some people like these products and I was hoping they would work for me, so I could get away from the products on the market that are polluted with chemicals, but this was a terrible experience for me. Back to the drawing board!

title: Very Disappointed - Sparkles Everywhere!
text:
-Most of the products in this set (blush and eye shadow) are VERY sparkly, which I did not expect and which I was specifically trying to avoid. They look like they would be very natural, neutral tones, but when you open the jars you can see they are full of glittery product. I wanted something I could use for a bridal look, and it is not recommended that you use something with glitter, as this can make your face look shiny and sweaty. When I put the blush on my face, it has exactly this effect - a very fake, overdone shiny look, even with just the smallest bit of the blush. So the blush is a total waste, and the eye shadows aren't much better.

-The foundation kind of comes on cakey even after using a very tiny bit, though I am hoping with practice I can apply it more effectively, since I am not very familiar with mineral foundations.

-The makeup did not last on my face all day, even though I used the mineral veil finishing powder and the spray that is supposed to help it stick.

-There is not a ton of pigment to these colors. The eye shadow that looks like it would be a warm brown is so light that it barely adds any color to my skin, and I have very light skin. It just looks like it smoothed out my natural skin tone. I guess if you are looking for that, fine, but don't expect it to look much different than a nude.

-The containers do not come with a plastic guard that a lot of powders come with to keep them from coming out too fast, so it is hard to tap out the right amount of powder into the very TINY cap without making a mess and wasting makeup.

Overall, very disappointed, although I will keep practicing on off-days to see if the foundation, bisque, and mineral veil are still usable.

I didn't buy from this Amazon vendor and am still in the installation process. This is what I feel about this product so far:

I had to put the frame up to understand that it requires 60X32 finished space to host the unit. Essentially treat it like a washer/dryer.
4) The drainage design is not American standard, and I was told it's European. The drainage pipe is only 1 1/2" (American uses 2" pipe) and no clear instruction in the menu on drainage hookup or choices of rough in preparation. The flexible drainage pipe looks cheap and I am not sure how long it will last before leaking.

I'll update you once the unit is finished and tested. Oeverall, the price seems really attractive. I recommend to have an experienced guy, which is hard to find, to put it together.

The contractor just got the installation 95% done. The unit looks beautiful. Everything works. I didn't regret the purchase, and feel the manufacturer should improve the product, especially installation manual, to deserve more stars.

title: I finally found a nice, quality large size clip!
text:
I've been happy with this clip. The spring on my old Goody clip finally bit the dust and finding a quality replacement in a large 5 inches size is quite challenging. I find that most clips nowadays are made with a brittle type of plastic that when I inevitably drop it on my tile floor, a tooth or two on the clip can easily break off. This clip seems to be made of the more pliable or soft plastic like my old Goody clip was made of - so drops don't result in a tooth shattering off the clip. I also really like the low profile of the tabs for your fingers on the back of the clip - they don't protrude nearly as much as on a regular clip and I like that. I also like the tortoise shell color - it blends in well with my hair color. I was willing to pay for a quality clip that would last and I am happy with this purchase. I like to have a few around the house for whenever or wherever I need them (cooking in the kitchen, in the bathroom for brushing teeth/washing face, in my suitcase, etc.) I will definitely be buying a couple more.

UPDATE: July 2019 - I still really like this clip and use one every day (I own several) however I've now had two break within a couple of months of purchase. One was at 3 months and one at 8 months. I can't remember what broke on the first one but this last one the spring didn't break - it was the plastic that holds the spring that twisted and will no longer hold the spring (see photo.) I love these clips because I have very long hair and they do hold my hair, but at $10 each I wish they lasted longer than 3 or 8 months. I had a Goody clip that lasted at least 15 years before it finally failed (spring broke) - too bad Goody no longer sells the super large clips. 3 stars off for the poor durability of this product.

title: Doesn't do anything that a reused margarine tub doesn't do
text:
Thanks to a series of unfortunate events involving a car accident AND a bike accident, I am the (not so) proud owner of a partial denture. For quite a while, I just used two old margarine tubs to soak my denture. (Pro tip: soak your denture in plain water in a separate container and then rinse it thoroughly before putting it in the cleaning solution, and then your cleaning solution won't get nasty.) But when the lids of my margarine tubs started to crack, I decided to get some "real" denture cups. Yeah...I should have just eaten some more margarine and washed out a new tub.

These cups are not in the least impressive. The lid of the blue cup snaps shut but isn't remotely leakproof--tip it just slightly and you'll have water or cleaning solution sloshing all over. The lid of the white cup doesn't even snap shut. It just barely rests on top of the cup and strainer, and if you don't watch what you're doing when you pick up the container, you'll find yourself holding the lid and looking at the cup and water/solution all over the floor. Furthermore, the two cups are far too hard to stack. The white one can't go on top of the blue one because the lid of the blue one is curved, but putting the blue one on top of the white one is precarious because the blue one is wider. And I find it surprisingly annoying to have two containers that won't stack taking up twice as much space as necessary in my tiny bathroom. About the only feature of these cups that is at all handy is the little strainer thing, and since my denture is plastic and floats, I don't find even that feature very useful.

Bottom line: you can soak dentures in pretty much any container, and you can find two small plastic containers with flat tops and secure lids for considerably less than the cost of these. Toast with margarine, anyone?

text:
I really wanted to like this product, and I love pineapple, so I was super excited when it arrived. Unfortunately, I was let down by the quality of the actual products. They make a cute gift set, but that's really all they have going for them.

I love the smell of pineapple, but I found the scent of these products to be unpleasant. They smell very cloyingly sweet and artificial, and not much like pineapple at all. The whipped body soap had a nice texture, but it left my skin dry, and it took a lot of product just to get clean. The body butter felt sticky and greasy, and not all that luxurious. My skin was left a bit tacky, and not very moisturized even after it was absorbed. The bath soak is alright, but it has the same unfortunate scent as the other products, and you really don't get much product, so it's more appropriate for foot soak than a bath. The body scrub was probably the best product out of the bunch, and it creates a nice lather when mixed with water. It left my skin soft, but unfortunately was also quite drying.

Overall, I can't recommend this product. The presentation of the product is adorable, and I love that it's vegan... but the quality of this skincare product set just isn't very good.

I really only got this device because I wanted to avoid the bloody mess of shaving with a razor.

Here's the truth... there is really no device that can provide short-cuts or easier methods when it comes shaving your head bald. text:
I have no idea whether this product works, but that's only the part of the reason why I am giving this only 2 stars.

I'm an older guy who still has bad acne scars from my teens and 20s. The prospect of owning a product that might help make some of those scars less visible was appealing, thus I purchased it.

It came well-packaged - but with no instructions. Other than deodorant and cologne, some men might buy moisturizer, but most don't know facial products as well as women know theirs. I'd already received a "Did you receive our product?" email, and I decided to respond. I informed the vendor that I did receive the product - but knew nothing about how to apply it. I asked whether only a drop was needed and spread around, or if a greater amount should be applied. I asked about "How much should I apply - liberally, or just a small drop? ...Leave on the surface of the skin, or rub it in? Use once a day, or more than that? ....if so, Should I wash my face before applying a second application?" I actually apologize in the email for asking these questions, but expressed that I wanted to do everything possible in hopes the product would work.

That was on 12/26/2016. On 1/3/2016, I contacted Amazon Customer Service to indicate I had not received a response. They wrote a second follow-up letter, and told me to give it 2 business days. As I write this review, it is now January 9th, and I've received 2 more follow-up "Are you liking our product?" emails, including one which assured me that if I had any questions to simply get a hold of them.

Today I called Amazon Customer Service again. They suggested I post a review which might catch the attention of the vendor. Considering their email said I simply had to get a hold of them, I'm appealing to New York Laboratories to get in touch with me via the emails which even Amazon has copies of, or post something and tell me where it is - but selling something applied externally to the skin without specific directions is not a respectable practice.

Here is what is posted on Amazon for this product:

About the Product
New York Laboratories Acne Scar removal Cream formulated with EGF Peptide-Cytoknol® revitalizes, promotes skin repair, smooths acne scars, fine lines and wrinkles while soothes and moisturizes
Cytokinol® - Stimulates inter-cellular communication, restores optimal cytokine balance for proper skin metabolism and repair, strong epidermal repairing effect, soothing, anti-inflammatory
SAFETY WARNING: For external use only. Rub a very small amount on the inside of your elbow area to test for any allergic reaction before use. Avoid contact with eyes, keep out of the reach of children. If pregnant, consult with your health care provider before use.
rh-Oligopeptide-1 (EGF) - Peptide, helps accelerate the growth of epidermal cells, reduce wrinkles and assist in wound healing. Adaptonyl® (Withania Somnifera (Indian Ginseng) Root Extract) - Regenerates cells stressed by external conditions, inhibits MMP activity, reinforces skin protective systems, restructures and promotes repair of skin barrier function, contributes to cutaneous homeostasis
Purchase with complete peace of mind, we are confident we have developed the absolute best Acne Scar Cream in the market. If you are not completely satisfied with New York Laboratories Acne Scar Cream, we will refund your entire purchase.

New York Laboratories: I request that you provide specific details about the product use of Scar Removal Cream.

Thank you.

title: Just can't do its job
text:
I want to believe in a world in which redemption is always possible. There should be no unforgivable sins; your better qualities should always offer the hope that your failings, however profound, can be overcome.

But this shaver fails in the single unforgivable way that an electronic device can: despite lots of bells and whistles, it doesn't do the one thing you purchase it to do.

I bought this to replace an older model Norelco wet/dry shaver that finally gave up the ghost. This razor offers some additional features my old one lacked: it's much lighter, holds a charge longer, and has a silly and totally unnecessary shave-goo-dispensing system built into it. I tried to find a wet/dry Norelco shaver with no "moisturizing system," but to no avail. If you want to shave in the shower, Norelco wants to insure you keep purchasing more shave gel cartridges. After reading some reviews that suggested the shaver worked perfectly well without it squirting glop everywhere, I was satisfied this was the right purchase.

Unfortunately, the shaver is unsatisfactory in one way: it just doesn't shave very well. I've used it on my face and head, with and without moisturizer, wet and dry, and its shave is pretty lousy. My old Norelco provided a shave that was very smooth and comparable to a blade; with this model, there's noticeable beard fuzz left behind immediately after I shave, and by the end of the day, I look like I forgot to shave at all that morning. When I found myself going back over my face with a regular razor right after I used the 8040X, I knew this shaver had to go. I would like to believe that its lightweight, comfortable form and good battery life could redeem it, but sadly, its transgression is too profound. I may not be able to forgive it, but I'm pretty sure I'll forget I ever owned it before long.

title: Great Idea; less than pleased with execution

I've had this diffuser on my desk for almost exactly 30 days. I have used it nearly every day as well. The Oscillation was a neat feature -- but I have just disabled it. For some reason it has started squeaking at one point after it has moved all the way to the left and has started its right-ward movement. Rather disappointing that one of the key "features" is basically dead on arrival. Failing after <30 days is not acceptable by any measure.

The rest of the features are pretty good and it does a great job with an area that is approximately 30x14. The interval mode does seem to work very well all things considered and a single "fill" lasts from Friday evening through Sunday --- used mid-afternoon till around midnight each day.

I am unsure if I would purchase it again. I have the Jasmine at work and it has been flawless. Although I supposed that should be expected -- it has fewer moving parts.

Update 2020/01/22: I'd have to say at this point -- I wouldn't buy one with the oscillation again. It seems that feature has marginal benefits and if it fails can be pretty frustrating. text:
I love the idea of earring backs that don't allow your earring to 'droop'. I also like the heart design and thought that it would be cute front or back. That's the only real positive I can say for these.

I tried them with six pairs of different length earrings and they only worked for one and not well at that.
- Studs were the only one it worked with and the earrings weren't heavy to begin with and didn't 'droop'
- heavier drop earrings didn't work with the straight post back because I couldn't get the heart shape to lay flat on the back of my lobe to make it not 'droop'
- heavier drop earrings with a hook back didn't work because there was no way to push the heart backing up and around the hook shape. I tried them with Kendra Scoot earrings, heavy Lucky earrings, some Belk sterling silver earrings and some very heavy Betsy Johnson ones. When the back of the earring was a hook it just wasn't working.

Bottom line, it worked for the lightest pair of earrings I owned and only because they had a straight post backing. I also had to constantly fuss with them since the opening (back of the hearts) couldn't be too tight or too wide. So I was constantly trying to manipulate them with my small long nose pliers.

Also, the price is ridiculous. Yes, it comes with two pairs, but you'd think one of them would be silver and one would be gold. Also, it's way too much money for something that doesn't do what it says it's going to do and has to be constantly tightened or loosened. I love the idea. I really do, I wear super heavy earrings (one of the reasons I got a second hole to begin with) But this needs work. It should be easier to use and should work with hook type backs because most heavy earrings are going to have a hook back.

title: Good features; disappointing results
text:
I have had this razor for 6 weeks now (that's past the 3 week adjustment period) and overall I am disappointed with it.

First, what I like about the razor:

The quick rinse cleaning is a very nice feature and the reason why I choose this razor. I am not very good about cleaning the razors.

The trimmer is on a spring release that works much better than my old Norelco's trimmer that took some force to open.

Indicators to let you know when to recharge and when the razor is at full charge.

What I did not like about the razor:

For the other posts who said the larger blades did not seem to make a difference from older razors, I must agree.

The charger light is only a light, not a gauge.

On the subject of charging, the manual says that you should not let the razor sit in the charger to preserve the internal battery. This can be a real problem since I shave close to the time I am leaving. So, I don't have the time to wait and remembering to charge it when I get home usually doesn't happen.

Although quiet (something that I could not care less about) it feels weak. I find myself constantly checking to see if it needs recharging. My problem areas were not solved by this newer razor with larger blades and my shaving time was not reduced.

Better make sure you are happy with your shave before rinsing the razor.

I find it works great if I skip a day of shaving, but daily shaving and 2 days or more of growth can give this razor trouble.

title: Not Great for Thick/Wavy Hair. Pretty & OK for Touch-Ups
text:
My whole life I've needed to use a hair straightener. I have very thick strands of hair and a lot of it. Plus, my hair is poofy crazy curly. My hair used to be down to my butt, however, this past year I had to cut it all off due to getting a horrid matted mess. (If you don't know what it means to have matted hair - your lucky). It was a whole bunch of tears, pain, tantrums, home remedies, a ton of hair salon visits and a ton of money spent until realizing that I was s*** outta luck and had to cry as they cut my hair to only an inch in the back, but luckily had enough hair left / saved on top and on sides for shoulder length hair. So now more than ever, having short hair that's very thick and curly, I'm always looking for amazing hair straighteners and products in general.

I have wanted one of these heat and style brushes and finally decided to test this one out. I loved the color of this heat brush and it looked like a nice, high quality hair straightening brush in the images.

This brush has less options then I thought it would. I cannot control the temperature and I would like for it to get a little bit hotter. Since I have curly, wavy hair this doesn't heat up enough to get it straight. Or maybe it's not doing a great job because it doesn't have two "plates" like regular straighteners. If I straighten my hair with a flat iron, this is a great touch up tool for the days following the flat iron before I wash my hair again. SO - It does work, but it is NOT a miracle product. This hair straightening brush (& all brush type of straighteners) MIGHT work better / work faster / have better results if you have thin hair? Just a assumption.

One difference I noticed was the way my hair felt after styling with the Envy brush. When I use my flat iron, my hair is...flat. The flat iron leaves my hair very smooth but it doesn't seem to have much texture or body left after straightening. When I used the Envy brush, my hair was straight, but still had plenty of volume. I'm really happy I bought the Envy styling brush. I really like the volume my hair has after using this brush.

I had to completely comb through my hair to smooth it out before using this brush (obviously). I started out by just running the Envy brush through my hair. Once I was done brushing my hair, I sectioned off my hair for the best results. I sectioned off the top 2/3 of my hair, twisted and secured it to the top of my head. As always, I focused on the underside first. When I finished the under layer, I moved on to the middle section, and then the top. The whole process took me about 20minutes. Pretty close to the same amount of time that it takes me to use my regular flat iron.

An ion is as an atom in which the number of electrons and protons are not the same. When a hair tool has ionic in its name, it means that it can generate negative ions. Hair has high water content, making it positively charged. When negative ions come in contact with hair, the positive charge is neutralized. This leaves your hair straight, sleek, shiny and smooth.

Here is one crucial thing to keep in mind – not all flat irons are pure ceramic, many of them are aluminum. They are just coated with ceramic on the top. Such models are less expensive, but you need to be extra careful when using them. This coating can chip or peel, revealing less quality metal below. These peeled areas can snag your hair! So always try to find out if an iron is coated or not.
You can even find costly professional models that are not 100% ceramic. Solid or pure ceramic are words that you are looking for.

I'm not sure if this brush is ceramic, titanium or what..?!?

Titanium vs. Ceramic
In this battle, it is obvious that titanium is a winner. But does this mean that you should use only this type of iron? No. Many experts say that consumers should use ceramic for one obvious reason. Since titanium can get very hot and transfers heat better, it’s very easy to damage your hair if you are not careful. Also, this high heat is only advantageous for women with thick, coarse and stubborn hair. If your have thin or fragile hair, there is no need for high temperatures. In the end, it is up to you to find out what will work best for your hair. Now you have all the facts to make the right decision. If you are still indecisive, there is a simple solution! Get a flat iron that combines ceramic and titanium, such as Croc 2 Infrared mentioned above. This way you get ceramic’s safety and protection and titanium’s speed and efficiency.

title: Length is not uniform, very thin on bottoms.
text:
I bought these I-tip hair extensions to replace some thinning patches I have on my head. I have had hair extensions professionally put in from my hairdresser in the past and she suggested I stick with the I-tip, primarily for the ease of use and convenience. I was hoping it would save some time and money being able to add some volume to my thinning spots. I received them promptly and they looked and felt soft and silky. The ends were quite thin and wispy. I ordered the 18” and felt like I only got about 14” of quality hair. The color selection are very good and accurate. I was able to match it perfectly with my own hair color. I also liked the fact you can color you hair with them in.
With these extensions you have the option of glueing them in or using the beads to clamp them in. I chose the beads. One of the first things I noticed was how thick the tip of the hair piece was with glue. Being that I have thinning hair you can see the bead and tip at times. Note.. If you blow dry your hair with the heat setting too high the pre-glued tips start to melt and get gooey.. even with the beads on. . After I applied some extensions in my hair I was excited I had hair that looked balanced and my thinning spots ( on sides of my head) looked fuller. It was great until I washed my hair. I followed the directions and was very careful combing them out. They started to frizz up and shed a little after my second wash. I was somewhat disappointed at that point. I hadn’t had that happen before. I could have made a little birds nest after a month. I did get my grow out (roots) colored and the color looked great on the extensions. I wish the hair pieces were a little fuller and the advertised length was really the true length. The issues I experienced is not with the seller but the manufacturer for not disclosing the fact it is synthetic hair. The price I paid is much less than others I noticed. You get what you pay for is my opinion.

title: Lot of hit and miss.
text:
[[VIDEOID:e6424147f4b4136bd53f39eb82f6fc17]] Pros:
Decent construction.
Cleans itself of fur pretty darn fast/easy.
Cover for the bristles is nice.
Removes some shed and combs hair.

Cons:
Packaging is cheap, half clamshell stapled to a cardboard backing. This isn't a big deal but it did result in the packaging being fairly mangled (like it had been tossed around at a pet store for way too long) and would look embarrassing if you purchased it as a gift. (This did not affect my score though, as it's just packaging)
So much retail space, probably 1/3 of which has no brush.
Bristles looked bent/misaligned right out of the package. Again kind of feels like maybe it was used (it looks super clean, but between the bent bristles and the mangled/stapled packaging I gotta wonder)
Doesn't feel like it's REALLY effective at thinning out the shedding fur. (it took quite a bit of brushing to get that wad in the video, and he's a 13-15lbs ginger-chonk.) With how hot it's been I was expecting a lot more shed out of him. Maybe he cleans himself really well and I don't realize it.

Verdict:
It's an adequate brush. The solid brush cover is great and the ease at which it cleans itself with the pull of the trigger is amazing. I do wish the brush head were a little smaller or there were more bristles covering all that brush head. Just feels like a waste. I'd also invest in better packaging and quality control (if that's really how the bristles come from the factory).

If you need a brush this will suffice (at least for short haired cats, I cannot attest for dogs or long haired cats.) Probably wouldn't be my first choice though.

title: Using this cleanser with Clarasonic
text:
For the price, I have to wonder why this item is not listed under Amazon's "luxury beauty" line. Like many reviewers, I was put off by the sheer amount of packaging that came along with this item. It wouldn't be so bad if they didn't tout how conscious they were of environmental issues, but I've purchased Chanel with less packing, come on!

All of the beauty and skin care products I consume are luxury, at the moment I've been using Dr. Gross's skin care line but until I could get back to Sephora, I've been using Purity cleanser. I was hoping this product would be a suitable replacement but I'm not convinced so let me tell you about the photos.

Each night I cleanse my face with Purity using Clarasonic's Uplift with the Revitalizing brush. I follow this with micellar water (by Borghese) and then a serum and moisturizer. The whole thing takes about 7 minutes (it's therapy, don't judge!).

Upon waking, I swabbed my face with the micellar water and then took a picture of the cotton ball along with an untouched cotton ball for comparison. And by the way for the uninitiated, micellar water is the best skincare product to come out since mascara was invented. I was sure that my $349 Clarasonic erased all traces of dirt no matter the soap, but the micellar water never lies.

On the second morning, first thing, I used the Clarasonic with the Radiance brush and three pumps of LaClaire Foaming Botanical Facial Cleanser. Two pumps did not create a bit of lather. Then using micellar water, I swabbed my face again and there you have the picture of both -- no cleanser and cleanser.

You can see that there is still a lot of dirt left behind after using this cleanser, certainly less than no cleanser at all but there is still some there. There is less dirt left after washing with Purity so I wouldn't call it a miracle cleanser, it's really just "okay."

title: Pretty Decent Set! Avoid If Sensitive to Smells!
text:
This is a pretty decent set! For $25.99 (at the time of writing this review), you get a lot of items!!

I love that it comes in a cute little caboodle box! Everything fits in it great! So all of the stuff is together in one place and it’s small enough that it’s easy to store!

The little pots of glitter cake together in a little zip lock bag, which I appreciated because some of the glitter had spilled out, so that kept it contained. It was only a few glitter particles, but I was still glad it was contained to the little bag! The poly gel tubes each come in their own little bags too, which I thought was nice. None of them leaked, but if they had it would have been very messy had they not been in a bag and still messy if they weren’t in separate bags. So, even though mine didn’t leak, I’m glad the company thought of the possibility and planned ahead just in case!

The polishes all come in their own box. I wish they would have labeled the OUTSIDE of the boxes. The only thing on the boxes were “Nail Polish” on 2 of them and “Gel Nail Polish” on the rest. Since 2 were supposed to be the top and base coat and only 2 said “Nail Polish,” I figured those were the top and base coats. I was wrong. I’m not sure why 2 said “Nail Polish” and the others said “Gel Nail Polish,” especially since they’re all supposed to be Gel polishes 🤷‍♀️ So, I had to open each box and look at each nail polish bottle to see which ones were which. The base and top coats were labeled on the outside of the bottles. BUT, the colored polishes weren’t labeled in any way. So the only way to figure out which color was which was to open each one. A minor inconvenience, but annoying when they could have just labeled them with the colors! So, I ended up putting a dot of the polish on the top of each box so I’d know in the future. It would just be nice if in the future the company labels them better!

The polish STINKS! It smells like burnt plastic 🤢 All Nail Polish stinks, but I’ve gotten used to the “regular” stink of nail polish. Smelling burned plastic while painting my nails is not something I’ve gotten used to! But, for the price of everything I got, it’s something I can deal with. But if smells bother you, this is not the kit for you!!!

The UV lamp works okay. I took a few times of turning it on to get the nails to dry, but it’s small so I wasn’t expecting too much and they did and it was still faster than if I painted my nails with regular polish and waited for them to dry. So I’m happy!

Overall, it’s a good little kit! I love that it comes all together in the cute little caboodle box. I love that you got an assortment of polish colors and an assortment of poly gel colors. I love that it came with the base and top coats. I love that it came with a UV lamp. I love it came with the tool needed for the poly gel nails. I love it came with glitter, foils, and strip tape to decorate the nails. I didn’t like that the polishes weren’t labeled better and I didn’t like the burnt plastic smell of the polish. But for everything I love and the affordable price for everything you get, I can get past those 2 things I didn’t like!!

I’d say the only thing that would make me tell you to avoid getting this kit would be if you’re sensitive to strong smells because of the burnt plastic smell from the polish. Other than that, I’d recommend this kit!!

title: Note that slices are not full masks
text:
Each pouch has 12 pineapple ring shaped slices you can stick on your face. It is not enough to cover my face and I can wear the average sheet mask.

If you have used circular cucumber eye masks that various brands make, you will find these masks to be similar. You are receiving small rounds in a packet rather than a full sheet mask.

However what is awkward is that unlike cucumber eye sheet masks, you get 12 slices rather than just 2. While this seems like it would be better, in reality is that means you need to commit to using all 12 slices of fruit in one go because there isn’t an easy way to reseal the mask package. It doesn’t come in a resealable pouch.

Because you end up with 12 slices of mask to use you end up covering maybe half your face with slices and you’re basically doing more for less mask. The instructions do say this mask can be used anywhere on the body but I don’t know how that would work in practice. What areas need sheet masking and where will the rounds stick?

I think if Kocostar had made the slice line of masks into a fruit salad deal with multiple slices of fruit per pouch that would’ve made more sense. If they had sold these masks as 12-120 rounds in a container like many eye masks are sold, that also would’ve made sense.

I think if you intend on sharing these masks with others (Eg six friends each taking a pair of slices) or want to store the opened packages or want to use masks to target specific areas of your face or body this could be a good purchase.

These mini masks were moisturizing but dried out faster than a full size sheet mask. I don’t know if that’s due to size or formula.

title: Nice strong scent at first, but it disappears very quickly.
text:
I really loved the idea of this Boiess Baby Cologne "Les Enfants" in White Blossom, and thought it would be perfect for myself since I don't like loud fragrances. The description of the scent profile really enticed me, as I love all of the notes. I was able to try both the White Blossom and the Lavanda scents.
Both of the "Cologne" sprays smell identical to me. I can't say that I can tell them apart at all. They both have a very strong earthy, herbal, slightly floral scent that is heavily ladened with alcohol upon spraying. It stays very strong for several minutes, but then starts to dry down.
Sadly, once it dries down, the scent pretty much dissipates. If I don't spray it heavily at first, which is too much for my asthma to handle, the scent just goes away completely. I must spray it on me again. Once I spray it on a few times over an hour or so, I can smell the ever so slightest hint of it on my clothing later, if I put my nose right on it. That is a lot of spraying for very little payoff.
I know this is meant for kids mostly, but I would think the scent would and should last longer. Sure, my grandsons will like using it, maybe, as it is quite strong at first. But, I think it would just be more for the fun of it and very short lived. This is also very expensive "Cologne" to not be able to smell it after 30 minutes, and right at $28 is too expensive for me to buy just for the fun of it.  
For others this "Baby Cologne" may be something wonderful or maybe they can smell it more than I can. As I said, I really love the idea of a light fragrance, but not for babies. I do wish the scent stuck around more for me.

text:
This is probably about the 100th brand I have tried for an eye mask if I exaggerate a bit.
I use under eye patches almost everyday, sometimes twice a day not only for under eye but also for my neck lines and forehead.
So I am not kidding when I say I have tried 10s of different brands of under eye patches from Amazon.
To be honest, under eye patches are for a rather temporary fix, in that you have to use them everyday or for a long period to have more permanent effects. But that’s how all skin care products work in my opinion. I use it to reduce very fine lines under my eyes (you can’t really see it unless you look in the mirror closely but it bugs me), and prevent my neck and forehead lines from getting worse (and hopefully to improve).
This one didn’t stay well at all on my neck, and I felt it dried out too quickly.
FYI, I don’t have dark circles, so my rate of effectiveness is solely for fine lines and such.
For my neck lines, I think most eye patches are at par in terms of quality, to be honest. Of course, from time to time, there are brands with quite inferior quality to others. I wouldn’t know about this one, as it kept falling off.
The last straw was that it just ripped apart when I tried to move the slipped mask back to the intended spot. It was annoying. After a couple of times, I just took it all off from my face.
The bottom line is that this product doesn’t have any price advantage to overlook its rather inferior quality compared to similar quality eye masks in this price range either.
I got so many other eye masks right now, I am not going to use this one unless I run out of eye masks between shipments or something (highly unlikely though).
Overall, 2.5/5 from me based on my experience of trying this mask for the very first time, and I won’t be recommending this.

A metal scraper doesn't really work with these, which is no big deal, but it's nice for people to know what they'll be getting. The plastic film is really hard to get off, so remember to be careful as these are just little discs of sharp metal.

=lots of images to choose from

=tip designs and single-image designs work well

CONS:
=full nail is WAY too small for normal nails
=some images are hard to pick up properly
=plastic film is really hard to remove
=edges are sharp

text:

The process was actually pretty fun. I’ve noticed people complain that it’s still sticky after using the LEDUV light, but I have found that I have to use the light about 3 times for each nail for it to fully cure. You have to apply it pretty thick for them to last a while. The thinner the poly gel, the more likely it will break off easier.

Results:
The results were very cute! The nails only lasted a couple of hours though as 2 nails broke off after I took a shower, but I have a feeling it was because it was my first time and I applied the poly gel fairly thinly.

Final thoughts:
All in all I would try it again and see how I do. It’s fun for someone who wants to try it out. It’s cheap, and if you know what you’re doing, it comes out pretty good.

text:
Got this as it looked like a good purchase. Still is, for the right person. I say that because of the following reasons:

Comb:
Pros: Wood comb is nice. A good size. Goes perfect in pocket if you do that. Seperates the facial hair easily, no snags. (Actual teeth usage size is 85MM, with them being ~2MM apart)
Cons: Can break as it's wood. (Not really a bad thing, but must mention.

Pen: (Opened, but did not use, nothing to say on this)

Brush:
Pros: Solid wood handle. Bristles are a good length of ~18MM tall. Coverage of brush is ~100MM from one point to the other long way, and ~50MM at the widest part.
Cons: Not really made for thick/long facial hair. Bristles won't touch skin, so you will only be brushing the 'top' layer. When looking at them in mirror, they bend a little too easy, so they are not really stiff.

Overall: Maybe a great feel for someone with a not too thick/long beard. Comb feels good as well. (Did not use pen, so nothing to say there).

title: The loofah does not cover the full LENGTH of the strap.
text: Well, I WAS warned.  Another reviewer complained that the loofah covered only one third of the strap.  I mistakenly took that to mean one third of the width, not one third of the length.  Looking at a picture of the product posted by a different reviewer, I could see no indication of that characteristic.  I concluded that the critical reviewer must have either received a defective product or that the product had been redesigned subsequent to that individual’s procurement.  Upon receipt of my own, I now see my error.  The loofah portion only covered the center third lengthwise.  This, coupled with the generous overall length of the strap (which the company dubiously touts as a selling point), means that anyone who is not tall will be tasked with having to try to extend both arms full-length in order to get the truncated loofah portion of the strap to reach desired areas, a problem exacerbated by the narrow design of most modern tub/showers.  This is a design oversight.

title: Painless and easy to use, but the device gets super hot
text: I have been using this hair removal device for 2 months now. I used it once every 2 weeks so I've used it 5 times so far. Now, the sessions will be only once a month until all the unwated hair is removed. The manufacturer recommends using it once every 2 weeks for the first 5 sessions and then once a month after that, so using it multiple times a week won't change the outcome. The areas I use this device are my legs, under arms, bikini area and upper lip. The only difference I've noticed so far is the upper lip hair. It is growing significantly less, like almost 90% is gone. The rest of the body hair still grows the same amount, but the hair started to grow softer. I assume the hair is finally becoming weaker. I am half Greek and half Italian, I have olive skin color with dark hair, so it might take over a year for me to see some results. Overall, the device is very easy to use and it is painless, but it gets super hot to the touch after about 5-10 minutes of continues usage. I use the device on my legs first and then take a break until it cools down, and then I continue using it on other parts of the body and stop to cool it down again. I have to admit it is frustrating to stop the session to cool down the device. I don't know if other hair removal devices get this hot. This is my first time using something like this so I can't compare.

title: It only made my hair a little softer....
text:
I bought this at Sally Beauty. I am caucasion, in my 50's with blonde/gray fine hair that is straight with some body & has never been colored or bleached; length is 2" below my shoulders.
My hair has been very dry for a long time despite lots of moisturizing, a salon keratin treatment (cha-ching!), argon oil, deep conditioning, etc... This Aphogee two-step protein treatment was recommended to me at the Sally Beauty store, and I figured it was worth a try. I followed the instructions to a T & also watched lots of youtube videos. I used this today exactly as directed & with high hopes. I shampooed & towel-dried my hair, then applied protein treatment, blow dried my hair for 12 minutes w/ the protein treatment in it, then rinsed in shower with warm water followed by the balancing moisturizer for at least 2 minutes, rinsed & used a moisturizing hair mask ("Mystic Divine" Coconut Complex Hydrating Masque), then rinsed again. My hair felt softer, at first, but my frizzies & curly gray hairs are still sticking out all over. I didn't get any more body in my hair either (my keratin treatment was last year 2017). So, all in all it is okay as a moisturizer, but no better than a regular deep moisture conditioner or mask. I'm not sure if I would use it again, maybe. I'm glad I just got the sampler size.
Here are my tips:
1) Use a spray mister bottle for the protein liquid & make sure you get out every last drop from the packet because most of it came out as beer colored water, then at the bottom of the packet was more of a thick cream, so I shook them together in the spray bottle & I'm so glad I used that! Don't just pour it on your head, at the very least pour a little into your hands at a time (after massaging the packet to mix contents) and smooth through your hair that way. There was just enough for my hair length.
2) Don't put a towel or anything around your shoulders, no clothing either because the protein treatment will dry your hair to it. Don't pull your stuck hairs off your skin, they'll come unattached in the shower, no worries. I kept my hair behind me to apply treatment & blow dry.
3) After drying the protein into your hair, don't touch your hair or bend it, (you can very gently touch lightly with your finger, if you hair wasn't already super brittle; it will feel like plastic sort of. 4) Be very careful blow-drying; I pointed the dryer downward alternating between medium & high heat & kept it farther from my hair so it wasn't blowing it around as it hardened. When hair is totally hard & dried through then gently let the shower water fall over all of your hair until you feel no more stiffness, then you can condition.
It's worth a try! The packets were just under $4 at Sally Beauty if you want to try it, or order here on Amazon.

title: Mediocre masks. Factory errors.
text:
Man, I got these cheap at a store near me and I’m glad I did! They absolutely are not worth the price they’re charging online! I paid $1 for one and it was buy one get one free. So 50 cents per mask. First off, maybe it was a factory error, hence the cheap price, but the tea tree and calendula smelled exactly the same! I have pure tea tree oil at home, so I know what it’s supposed to smell like. I did like the calendula mask, pleasant floral scent and very moisturizing. Definitely not for my oily skin type, but dry skin users will definitely benefit! There’s a lot of essence left in the packets after using the masks, so I saved it by rolling them up and closing it with a clip. It could last over 8 uses for facial applications! I also used it as a body lotion to great success.

Lotus and hibiscus were nice, moisturizing masks with pretty scents. Again, too greasy for my skin, but that’s not a point against them, it’s just not right for me personally.

The biggest issue was the rose hip one, which really disappointed me because I love rose scents. This smelled nothing like a rose, it smelled like glue! Very non irritating and moisturizing, but unattractive smell.

Another big issue with these is they expire within a year of their manufacturing date! So depending on when you get it, you’re rushing against the clock to use it before they go bad.

Beautiful packaging and generous essence portions, but with the issues I mentioned and the fact that besides being moisturizing they didn’t do much else, they very average in quality.

title: Great trimmer
text:
I've had this trimmer for probably 6+ years and it is still going strong. Just a hint if you have one and are looking to replace the G380 due to battery loss give this a try once a year:
Run until the battery discharges fully. By this I mean when the battery is getting weak I take the attachments off and turn on the power switch. Leave the switch on until the gizmos stop rotating then turn off. Wait about 20 minutes or so and then power on to deplete the rest of the battery (you can try this a few times to make sure it is fully drained). After discharging, plug it into the charger and let fully charge (I think I let mine charge overnight). This unit is now back to original power, and I haven't had to recharge in over 3 weeks of normal use and it functions like new). Just a tip to save you some money before deciding to buy another unit which I almost did. I could not find a replacement battery when I thought the battery was the issue.

title: Pretty good mild cleanser, but not a one-and-done type product.
text:
I have been using this Isabel Fay deep cleansing rose hip seed facial cleanser gel for over a month now, and I do like it quite a bit. I love the minimal ingredient list (Purified Water (Aqua), Sodium Olivate, Glycerin, Rosa Rubiginosa (Rose Hip) Seed Oil, Eriobotrya, Japonica Extract, Chondrus Crispus (Seaweed) Extract).

This product seems to be all around quite mild. The scent is lightly floral, not overly pleasant or unpleasant, not too strong and doesn’t linger. The lather is present but not super foamy. Most importantly for me, the product has not CAUSED any irritation. I have really sensitive skin, and I have not noticed any additional drying or breakouts due to using this product. However, I also haven’t noticed any particularly hydrating or clearing effects either. My skin does feel rather smooth and fresh since using this wash, but I find that I still need several other facial products to achieve this.

I was a bit concerned with the directions stating to avoid the eye area, because many of the healthy-skin and anti-aging benefits of the ingredients in this product would be ideal for the eye area, and I was initially hoping to use this as a make-up removing cleanser. However, I adhered to the directions, and I do not use this as a make-up removing cleanser, and only use it following or prior to make-up removal/application. The good news is, while I don’t directly put this product on my eyes, I am not super careful about avoiding the eye area while rinsing and I have not experienced any stinging or eye discomfort as I have with several similar products in the past.

Overall, I found this to be a pretty good product, I like it quite a bit but I didn’t find it to be a particularly extraordinary product either. I do recommend this product to others as a part of their beauty regimen, but I definitely need (and recommend others) to use a make-up remover prior to use, and a moisturizer following use, so this isn’t a one-and-done type product.

title: Like many "mature adults"
text:
Like many "mature adults", it seems that I grow nose hair faster than any other hair. Ugh! I had a little miniature clipper years ago, and it sat in the damp bathroom and the battery rusted, so now it's "toast". Had always been fascinated by these little "finger powered" trimmers, but never seemed to come across one. Searched Amazon, and there it is! Looks exactly like I remembered from years ago, and inexpensive as well.

The quality and packaging are fantastic! Comes with a cleaning brush, a spring, and instructions. Packaging is very nice. Looks like it will last FOREVER. And, NO BATTERIES. Electric products that look a lot like this cost twice as much.

It requires a little bit of practice to use because everything is "backwards" looking into a mirror and holding the tool. Very sharp, and despite my clumsy hands, no nicks or scratches. Seems to be "idiot proof." I give it only four stars because despite hacking away for some time, I was never able to clip ALL of my nose hair. It doesn't show, but it's still pretty long in there and will reappear quicker than I'd like. Cannot imagine using it on "ear hair", because looking at my ears in the mirror seems too difficult. (Guess the lady who cuts my hair will continue to clean up that hair and trim my eyebrows. Ive never had the nerve to ask her to trim my nose!)

This quality for this price is still a GREAT DEAL.

title: Best Shaver I've Used So Far
text:
I'm almost 59 years old and have been using an electric shaver (almost always Norelco) since I started shaving at 13. I've been using this shaver for about a month. I find it gives me a much closer shave than my previous Norelco and is much faster to boot. I seem to average about 4 minutes for a shave. The display indicates 85 minutes of shaving on a full charge. When I got down to 7 minutes the display then rapidly counted down to zero, curious. The charging cord now has a small transformer lump on the outlet side making it bulkier than the cord only arrangement on my old Norelco. While a nice zippered case is provided for the shaver, there is no provision for packing the charger cord. The included stand seems a little flimsy. The manual warns not to keep the shaver plugged into the charger continuously or battery life would be shortened. The manual further warns that the shaver should be charged no longer than 1 hour after the initial 4 hour charge. I don't know why there couldn't be an electronic circuit to limit the charge without having to worry about causing battery damage. Cleaning the head is a simple matter of rinsing under hot water. I admit that I'm a hopeless techie and I do enjoy the digital display however if you wanted to save $50 you could get the model without it and still have much of the same functionality.

Bear in mind that satisfaction with a particular shaver is very subjective and variable. I have a moderately coarse beard and no significant ingrown hairs. My ethnicity is east European Ashkenazim. Your experience may vary.

title: Practice makes perfect
text:
My wife has always wanted to try magnetic eyelashes, so she decided to give these a shot. They really do work! But, with these practice makes perfect.

They come with 2 tubes of magnetic eyeliner (black), and 10 sets of eyelashes along with the application tool. When you apply the magnetic eyeliner, you have to be precise. The eyeliner is black, and will look very dark if you do too thick of a line. I would do thinner lines if possible, with about 2 layers so that the eyeliner is not overwhelming. Once the eyeliner dries, use the application tool to put the lashes on.

It does feel a bit strange at first (if false lashes are new to you), and it may tickle around your eyes when you blink. But yes, these really work! With more practice my wife will get better at this.

The only thing is that the magnetic eyeliner does not come off easily. You will need a good eye makeup remover to get this off as it’s waterproof!

title: Great for Goldens!
text:
Used for my 2 Goldens which shed a lot. They typically like to be brushed and don't mind the vacuum. We typically take them to the groomers every couple of months.

PROS: Did a great job brushing my dogs fur. The size of the brush was perfect for a medium/ large dog. (These bristles are not meant to tackle fur with knots and tangles.
I would pre-brush those out or the bristleswould bend.) My husband was worried that the way the attachments slid on that we would loose suction, but it was not noticeable. My canister was filled with hair that would have otherwise been all over the floor. I loved that when you release the brush, the hair sucks immediately into the vacuum. If you have a lot of hair coming off the dog, you don't have to worry about it getting on the floor.

CONS: The way this attaches to our vacuum makes it inconvenient for dog placement. The Shark has a handle which can get in the way. A hose attachment would have helped with being able to brush from any angle. You also have to be able to hold the brush down manually. Which is great for easy release of fur to be suctioned, but can make your hand tired for big/ multiple dogs. A locking mechanism option would be helpful.

With a hose and lock option this would be a 5 Star product.

I would recommend it for anyone looking for an handy, clean and quick way to groom their shedding dog!

title: Hopefully my honest review can improve future products and makeup brushes from a brand I love
text:
I will start of by saying Bella and Bear is an incredibly awesome customer-oriented brand that goes above and beyond when it comes to taking good care of their consumers. I have been a member of their beauty club, which I highly recommend. I have struggled to leave this review but honesty is the best policy. Hopefully my honest review can improve future products and makeup brushes from a brand I love so much.
I am not impressed with the Kitten set. Many of my friends raved about the Kitten makeup brush set and how much they loved it. The case is very stylish and classy. It is nice to have a sturdy leather case for my makeup brushes.

I wish the brushes were labeled – a pamphlet was included on using the brushes and their purpose. However, I wish the brush handles were labeled like it is done by some high end brands. A general consumer with less knowledge about cosmetics or brush usage will fumble around trying to figure out when to use a brush. I like the pamphlet. I found it neatly organized but it’s a piece of paper. I have no idea where it ended up.
A lot of the face and powder brushes are too identical. You don’t need that many face brushes that serve the exact purpose. Give me an angled brush or a foundation brush – all of these face brushes had the same purpose and it seemed wasteful.
The fallout – oh Lord, the fallout. I always wash my brand new makeup brushes with mild organic baby shampoo and let them air dry. I tested this before and after washing – the bristles fell out, but no excessively, as I was trying to apply makeup. One bristle got in my eye and I can’t describe to you the horrendous pain that causes. I had to be extremely careful to take the bristle out without stabbing my cornea.

It would be a far stretch to refer to these brushes as professional grade. They are great if you’re a makeup newb or trying to learn applications. The eye brushes blend very well. My eye makeup looked great – powder and blush were hit and miss. I think this set has a huge potential but lots of room to grow and improve. I'm leaving a four star review because of excellent blending and the case is truly fantastic to have.

I was fortunate enough to qualify for a discounted or free makeup brush set through the Bella and Bear beauty club giveaway.

I compared hers to this one and i think the shape of this facial brush is a lot more practical since it comes to that point at the top which is great around the eye, nose, mouth areas. However, looking at the Luna bristles and the bristles on this unit you can tell the Luna has their bristles closer and also has a great variety of brush levels which their claim is to more efficiently cleanse the skin meeting the specific needs of different facial areas... compared to the Sytles II, this unit only has 2 types of bristles. The Luna says it cleanses with 8,000 pulsations per minute, but this unit says it can "reach 32,000 times per minute massage design if high frequency vibration" ...which i'm not sure how true that is..and what that even means.... what is 32,000 times? What is it referring to?...this leads me to my other gripe with this product...........the instructions!!!!!!!!

I wish this unit had BETTER INSTRUCTIONS...I was reading it and i'm so confused - it doesn't say how many modes it has and what each mode is used for..but it mentions "modes" have eight gears?

Here's the "operation" instructions..please try to decipher what it means... and yes i know there's typos..but that is how it READS on the instruction manual..."each mode has eight gear, may adjust the intensity according to your needed. According to the intermediate key open product cleaning mode for the first tiem. According to the second closed products the intensity of each mode can be though the + and - buttons to increase"............excuse me what? anyway ...

Here are my instructions!!!
1.) Charge the unit to full before first use. Flashing means it's charging and when it stops blinking it is fully charged.

2.) Wet the unit and your face, apply some face wash and turn the unit on to cleanse your whole face for 2 minutes. This unit has 2 modes, cleanse and massage. When you press on the button between the - and + you have it on cleanse mode (the faster vibration) and you can adjust the vibration intensity higher or lower depending on what you prefer. When you press the middle button again it turns off ..when you press it one more time it will turn onto the massage mode (slower vibration) you can adjust the speed of vibration in this mode as well.
-The unit does NOT have a self timer so don't expect this unit to shut off after 2 minutes of cleaning. It also says it has "acoustic cleaning" which i thought meant it would beep every 30 seconds indicating you should move to another part of your face (ex. left cheek, right cheek, chin and then forehead - like the clarisonic does) but does NOT so you need to keep track of how long you want to wash your face for with this.

3) Shut the unit off when you're finished by clicking the middle button between the - and +. Pat the unit dry or leave it where it can air dry.

One thing i like about this type of facial brush is that you don't need to replace any brush heads on this unit - it makes for more hygienic. This Styles II facial brush also claims to reverse signs of aging and restoring youth in your skin. I'm only 27 so i can't really speak to this claim, i don't have may wrinkles but i hope this is a great start for preventative measures.

This unit also claims to be a durable travel sized facial brush - it feels very light weight which i like because i don't want a bulky unit, i really like that the cord is very small and doesn't need a stand charging unit like the clarisonic. I haven't used this enough to know how long one charge can hold but I'll let you know once i continue to use this consistently. Be sure to read the instructions because it says you NEED to charge the unit fully before your first use. When you plug it in you will see the light at the bottom to start flashing indicating that it is actively charging. I hope this unit will last forever as it claims - wouldn't that be AMAZING! :)

I've already used this unit last night and i can say that my face felt very smooth and clean afterwards. I think it really preps the skin well for your serums and treatments at night, which is KEY for those products to work. If you don't exfoliate and clean your skin - it won't allow your products to actively work!

I'm really excited for the 100% money back guarantee! I've only had this unit for one night so I don't know how i like it yet for the long term but I'm glad that this warranty is here in case it doesn't work well for my skin or if it breaks....

Pros:
• Compact and easy to travel with
• Cute color!
• Comes with a charging cable ...which it came with a case too.
• Waterproof so you can use it in the shower
• Rechargeable - you can see the image where I'm charging the unit and the light is blinking. Once it stops blinking i'm assuming that is when it's fully charged.

Cons:
• The plug for the adapter to connect seems like it could rip over time - you can see it in the picture, it's very flimsy...
• The user manual has very odd grammar and is hard to understand which side is for "massaging" and which side if for "cleansing". PLEASE edit your instructions so we all understand how to properly use it.
• Does NOT have a self timer and it does NOT beep to indicate when to move to another part of your face like the clarisonic or Luna do.

I purchased this product at a discounted price in exchange for a honest review. I love face products and purchasing things on Amazon so this is truly my honest review. I think this is worth the $40 price tag for what it does. All in all - the Styles II facial brush does clean the face well, the vibrations are something to get used to.

title: Works great for me -- I like the smell of the lotion, and the smoothness it brings to the shave
text:
This is another excellent shaving product from Philips -- it cuts like an ordinary shaver, but with the added benefit of lubrication that helps it to shave smoothly. My skin doesn't get irritated or dry, and the lubrication seems to help the shave to go more quickly. I've tried other brands of shavers and this one seems to work the best.

This package comes with a squeeze bottle full of a very pleasant smelling lotion, that you inject into the back of the shaver. Then, when you are shaving, you just press a button and it releases enough lotion to lubricate about one third of the face. When it starts to feel like a dry shave, you press the button again and finish up.

I have found that the amount of lotion you can inject into the shaver is enough for about 5 to 6 shaves. The shaver comes with a small sample bottle of the lotion -- and I guess one drawback is that you have to keep buying the lotion, unless you want to use this like an ordinary dry shaver. I've tried that too and it seems to work as well as any other shaver I've tried. I prefer, though, to use the lotion. It feels good and has a nice aftershave smell that my wife also likes -- that's good enough for me.

Because the system is water resistant, you can shave in the shower, and you can wash it off in water when you are finished. The extendable trimmer isn't very useful, but I've never seen a shaver where they are. It comes fully recharged and after about two weeks of using it about every other day it is still working well -- I haven't charged it yet. I do wish there was some kind of indicator on the unit that would let me know how much charge remains, but all in all I am quite happy with this.

title: This Mat Wins Over Bundle Monster, Ejiubas & Bliss Kiss!
text:
I have this mat, the Bundle Monster mat, and the Ejiubas mat, and this one wins first place in terms of overall quality! It drives me crazy that it doesn't have any black areas for stamping & whatnot (thus, the deduction of one star), but its value, its reasonably sized nail guides, and best of all, the softness of the silicone makes this one the superior choice in my opinion.

DESIGN

In terms of design, I believe the other two mats are superior over Uber Chic, although UC's isn't bad. Bundle Monster's Lotus Mat is my favorite, but I'm also partial to lotus flowers ;) Its nail guides are ridiculously large, though, but it *does* have black sections to practice on, so that's a huge plus.

The Ejiubas mat has a pretty cool & very unique layout compared to all other mats, with its nail sizing grids in both black and white, while still leaving plenty of empty space to work on.

One thing I do love about the UC mat is the amount of empty space it features. Some mats out there that I haven't mentioned here are SO busy with verbiage & useless "features" that it's a huge turn off. Less is definitely more!

VALUE

With regard to value, Ejiubas wins, hands down. I purchased mine for $13, and it came with a great little carry bag! Bundle Monster loses miserably in this category. And, Uber Chic falls somewhere in the middle, which makes its value "okay" in my opinion.

TEXTURE - THE DEAL-BREAKER!

The (negative) deal-breaker for me is the stickiness of the other two mats. And as a disclaimer, I'm using the word "sticky," although it's not literally sticky... Rubbery is probably a better word, but I'm going with sticky ;)

So, I can't stand how *everything* sticks to the Ejiubas mat to the point that you can't even blow or fan debris off of it with your hand. This means it always feels like it needs to be cleaned, it's difficult to keep clean, and actually cleaning it is kind-of a pain.

The Bundle Monster mat falls somewhere between Ejiubas and Uber Chic in terms of stickiness. It's much better than the Ejiubas mat, but still sticky enough to be plenty annoying.

The Uber Chic mat, though? It's heavenly smooth :) I love it! It's very soft, and very easy to keep clean. Absolutely zero complaints on that front.

CONCLUSION

If Uber Chic would add some black stamping sections, this mat would be absolutely flawless in my opinion. Every mat out there seems to have at least one superior and one inferior feature that makes it difficult to choose the "best" one.

If it were up to me, I'd use the Uber Chic mat with the Bundle Monster design, except with Uber Chic's nail guide sizes, and Ejiubas' price point & free carry bag. Maybe I'll just have to make one of these, so I can finally have the perfect silicone nail art mat! ;)

title: Just don't use the applicator in the tube!
text:
So, I had high hopes for this brow product. It DOES stay on -- but comes off as soon as you wash your face at night, so I'm not sure it's really as advertised. I secretly was hoping I'd only need to apply it every other day, but now I know that was unrealistic. The brow applicator in the tube is useless unless you want to go for the giant unibrow look (then by all means, go for it). When I first tried applying with the applicator I was Frida Kahlo's eyebrows on a fair-skinned blonde reincarnated and ready to write a scathing review. HOWEVER, using a **SMALL** makeup brush, this stuff goes on really easily without scaring my husband. I'm able to use it just to fill my brows in a little bit for a natural look, rather than pasting on a couple of caterpillars. And if I'm getting fancied up and want a bolder brow then I just go ahead and fill in a bit denser.

So, here's how you do it: take the applicator out of the tube, use a small makeup brush to wipe the product off the stick of the applicator, apply to brows and repeat (dipping the stick back in the tube) as needed. Voila.
-Jeff's wife

title: A must have for travel!
text:
Due to the nature of my wife's condition, we have to minimize the number of transfers to and from her wheelchair, so a shower chair is a must. The hospital already recommended the ShowerBuddy shower chair, while that has been invaluable, it's a beast in size and the hospital occupational therapist was unable to recommend a hotel solution. Thank goodness shortly after the Wheelable came on the market, a perfect solution for those who need a shower chair and want to be able to travel with it. It is ridiculously simple to set up and take down.

It's so convenient to have a chair that can fold and unfold with no assembly required, fits over even tall toilets and allows my wife to propel herself in it as she does with the ShowerBuddy Solo. It's also narrow enough to fit through those annoyingly narrow bathroom doors. Because of this, we were able to go stay at our favorite hotel at the beach that didn't technically have disability accommodations like wide door entrances and my wife was able to fully access the bathroom!

The only cons with this chair are the footrest and armrests, both of which are very short. Definitely get the footrest extension, otherwise you risk your feet sliding off the existing narrow footrest. The short armrests aren't a deal breaker, but for anyone with a spinal cord injury knows, it's all about being able to raise up in the chair when necessary. Hopefully there will be a solution forthcoming for the armrest as they did for the footrest...

Also, the pots of powder are kind of small to dip your nails in, but I made it work. I'd definitely purchase the powders again, I would love to see a powder and brush saver set! title: So far I’m impressed how well this holds without being sticky or tacky once dried!
text:
I just received this Hair Finishing Stick for fly-away strands of hair. So far I really like it. Surprisingly, it’s not sticky or tacky, even once it dried. It almost reminds me of the texture and consistency of a no water hand sanitizer. It basically has no scent, which I also really like. I have short hair but can push it behind my ears if I want. However, I have the little tiny hairs that are just too short to be held back by my ear and this is the main reason I wanted to try this. I normally would have to use so much gel or strong hairspray but then it looks wet and like I have too much product in my hair. When this dries, it really just looked somewhat shiny. I will still likely use some hairspray just to finish the overall hold and style.

Now for a few of the reasons I didn’t give it 5 stars but only 4. Although I absolutely love the ombré of pink into purple tub coloring, I would like something written on it anywhere to tell me exactly what the product is or instructions on the best way to use it (even if it was a sticker). Even on the box it came in, there isn’t enough information for me. I like to see the list of ingredients I’m using and if there is any caution on using it, say, near my eyes on my eyebrows (which I did try and it worked just like a decent eyebrow gel. It was able to kept my few unruly eyebrow hairs that always seems to grow the wrong way, in place). Perhaps because it’s made in China it doesn’t require that type of information as a product made in the US would require. Of course, that’s also why it’s very reasonable priced too.

All and all I will definitely continue to use this unless I see any adverse reaction or irritation on my skin or scalp. If that happens I will definitely update my review. If that doesn’t happen then I may have just found a new staple in my daily beauty routine!
